description: A publishing workflow spec defines the state machine for content lifecycle: states, transitions, roles, and approval requirements — enforced before any content type can use the workflow.

rules.description: A publishing-workflow-spec.spec.json must exist with non-empty states array, an initialState, and a roles object.
Workflow must include at minimum: 'draft' and 'published' states. A workflow without these states cannot represent the basic content lifecycle.
The 'published' state must transition to an archive or unpublish state. Published content without an exit path accumulates as stale live content.
Every declared state must be reachable from the initialState via transitions. Unreachable states are dead configuration that confuses editorial teams.
At least one terminal state must exist (published, archived, or any state marked terminal:true). A workflow with no terminal state has no definition of 'done'.
All role IDs used in allowedRoles or transitionRoles must be defined in spec.roles. Undefined roles cannot be enforced in the CMS.
Draft must not transition directly to published unless allowDirectPublish:true is explicitly set. Bypassing review means unedited content reaches live audiences.
